```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)
```

vapour reads vector *features* at a low level: geometry comes back as raw binary
(WKB) or as text, and attributes are read separately, leaving you to combine
them however you like. Part of that control is choosing *which* features to
read, rather than always pulling an entire layer into memory.

This vignette shows the four feature-access patterns vapour supports, using two
example data sources that ship with the package.

```{r setup}
library(vapour)

## a MapInfo TAB file of polygons (localities)
mvfile <- system.file("extdata/tab/list_locality_postcode_meander_valley.tab",
                      package = "vapour")

## a shapefile of points
pfile <- system.file("extdata/point.shp", package = "vapour")
```

Every feature has a positional *index* (0-based, in layer order) and a feature
*identifier* (FID) assigned by the driver. These are not always the same number.
The count of features in the layer is:

```{r count}
n <- length(vapour_read_names(mvfile))
n
```

## All features

Read every feature. The geometry readers return one element per feature, which
you pair with the FIDs or attributes as needed.

```{r all}
g <- vapour_read_geometry(mvfile)   # a list of raw WKB, one per feature
length(g)
g[[1]][1:8]                         # first bytes of the first geometry

## the matching feature identifiers
head(vapour_read_names(mvfile))
```

Extents and geometry types can be read the same way without decoding the full
geometry:

```{r all-extent}
str(vapour_read_extent(mvfile)[1:2])
table(vapour_read_type(mvfile))
```

## An index range, i to j

`vapour_read_geometry_ij()` reads a contiguous block of features *by position*,
from `i` to `j` inclusive (both increasing). Use `c(0, n - 1)` for all of them.

```{r ij}
ij <- vapour_read_geometry_ij(mvfile, ij = c(0, 2))   # the first three features
length(ij)
```

## Arbitrary indices

`vapour_read_geometry_ia()` reads features at *arbitrary* positions. Order is
respected and duplicates are allowed, so you can reorder or repeat features.

```{r ia}
ia <- vapour_read_geometry_ia(mvfile, ia = c(2, 0, 0))
length(ia)
```

## By feature identifier (FID)

Positional index and FID are not always aligned, so to select by FID use a SQL
query against the data source. SQL also lets you subset geometry and attributes
together with the same filter.

```{r fa}
sql <- "SELECT * FROM list_locality_postcode_meander_valley WHERE FID IN (2, 5, 9)"
wkt <- vapour_read_geometry_text(mvfile, sql = sql, textformat = "wkt")
length(wkt)
substr(wkt[[1]], 1, 50)
```

## Geometry as text

Any reader can return text instead of WKB -- GeoJSON (the default), WKT, GML or
KML -- which is convenient for inspection.

```{r text}
substr(vapour_read_geometry_text(pfile, textformat = "wkt")[[1]], 1, 40)
```

See `?vapour_read_geometry` for the full set of readers and the arguments they
share (`layer`, `sql`, `extent`, `limit_n`, `skip_n`).
